title: OpenAI Chat Completions handshake translator
creator: Ravi Desai
description: Implement a compatibility translation layer that accepts requests in the OpenAI Chat Completions shape and emits Redwood-native RPCs (and vice-versa) with correct semantics for streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. This ticket scopes the handshake/translation logic (request surface, streaming chunk framing, function_call <> tool invocation mapping, error mapping, and backwards-compatible fallbacks). The goal is to provide drop-in compatibility for customers using OpenAI-style Chat Completions while preserving Redwood runtime guarantees (latency SLOs, observability, safe fallbacks).
comments: 2025-01-16 - Ravi Desai: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed on two-stage translator (Request Normalizer -> Response Reconciler) to minimize downstream changes. Decided to keep mapping logic deterministic and idempotent to assist retries.

2025-01-20 - Marta Gomez: Prototype of request normalizer completed. Initial mapping rules: messages array -> Redwood.messages, role mapping preserved; 'name' on messages is preserved and becomes metadata.name. Functions array -> Redwood.tools with signature hashing. Added canonicalization for function param schemas (sort keys, remove $schema fields).

2025-01-23 - Design review (Alyssa Park): Approved approach for structured-output mapping using a 'json_schema' content type translation. Design requested explicit rejection behavior when model returns invalid JSON for a declared schema; we will surface a structured 'schema_violation' outcome with diagnostic tokens and model chunk offsets.

2025-01-28 - Engineering sync (Ethan Cole): Streaming semantics decision: translate OpenAI 'delta' chunks into Redwood token events but include an envelope field 'oa_chunk_type' so downstream observability can correlate. For function outputs streamed as 'tool' content, emit intermediate 'tool_partial' events and a final 'tool_complete' event with the full arguments object. This preserves incremental UI and debugability.

2025-01-31 - Security review note (Jian Li): Raised KMS/PII concern about function arguments streamed in cleartext. Mitigation: mark tool invocation streams with 'sensitive': true and ensure optional redaction hook in private deployments. Follow-up epic created (ENG-78021).

2025-02-02 - QA (Lina Moroz): Added tests to conformance harness: end-to-end tests for (1) streaming text generation with midstream cancellation, (2) function_call where model requests a tool and returns JSON arguments, (3) structured output with declared json_schema and a malformed model response. All tests currently passing on the prototype harness with small Llama backend.

2025-02-02 - Marta Gomez: Open PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/11234. PR includes translation layer, new telemetry tags (oa.compat_version), and a conformance test suite under infra/tests/compat_openai_cc/.
acceptance_criteria: Requests in OpenAI Chat Completions v1 shape are accepted by the Redwood front door and invoke the same routing/quotas as Redwood-native calls.
Streaming token deltas from models are emitted as Redwood streaming events with oa_chunk_type metadata and reassembly yields identical final text to the OpenAI-shaped response.

Function_call events map to Redwood tool invocations: name, arguments (JSON) and streaming partials are preserved; final tool result surfaces as a tool_complete event and as the content field in the reconciled response.
Structured outputs declared via function return or via content schema are validated server-side; schema violations produce structured diagnostic events and do not crash the runtime.
Compatibility layer is covered by conformance tests and documented in the platform dev guide and console integration docs.
Performance: translation overhead adds <2% median p50 latency at benchmark load and memory overhead per-request <4MB for typical 2k token runs.
implementation_notes: We will implement translator as a pluggable middleware in the request ingress path so Dedicated/Private customers can opt-in or out via config.
Prefer zero-copy framing for streamed bytes where possible. Use sequence numbers to guard against out-of-order event delivery when reconstructing function arguments.
Telemetry: add oa.compat_version and oa.mapping_strategy tags; emit metrics for schema_violation_count and tool_stream_partial_count.

Fallback behavior: if incoming request asks for an OpenAI-only feature we can't support (e.g., certain edge-case streaming flags), return an enhanced 400 with a compatibility_hint field explaining the gap and a recommended Redwood-native equivalent.

Test plan: unit tests for field mappings, property-based tests for message permutations, and end-to-end conformance tests against the compatibility harness. Add a Golden file set derived from live OpenAI responses.
Rollout plan: feature-flag behind 'openai_compat_v1' default off for new clusters; enable progressively for Canary -> Beta -> General after perf/regression checks.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Streaming reassembly bugs can cause truncated function arguments leading to tool mis-invocations. Mitigation: add sequence checks, checksum of assembled JSON, and fail-fast with diagnostics on checksum mismatch.

Risk: Users rely on subtle OpenAI framing semantics (e.g., multiple function_call suggestions). Mitigation: document differences and provide an opt-in strict compatibility mode that accepts multiple function_call suggestions but only forwards the highest-confidence one with a warning tag.
Risk: Sensitive data in streamed tool args. Mitigation: mark streams as sensitive and wire redaction hooks for private deployments; add KMS key usage audit for tool invocation payloads.
